title: Door log
html:
Every badge reader writes a line when someone holds a badge against it. This is the log of that evening.

Exhibit PDU/02door_log.csvevery badge swipe of the eveningDownload

One line from the log, from earlier that evening:

event_iddatetimezonedirectionbadge_idresult
DOOR-00042026-11-1318:05:10SECinB-190granted

Badge B-190 entered zone SEC, the security control room, at 18:05:10, and the door opened.

  • direction in: somebody entered that zone. Leaving most rooms needs no badge, you press a button. Those lines have an empty badge_id.
  • result granted: the door opened. denied: it stayed shut.

Find every badge that opened the door to the service corridor between 20:30 and 21:00.

The door log only has a badge_id, not the person. To get the employee ID, find that same badge_id in staff.csv: the row it is on is the employee.

prev_card.title: Forty employees, four suspects
prev_card.html:
Four people could open G4 and SC and were at work during the speeches: Elena Petit (curator), Julien Moreau (security supervisor), Maya Chen (conservator), Thomas Lefebvre (logistics coordinator).

Your filter was a query: a question you ask a table, here G4 and SC, at work from 20:30 to 21:00. A database writes the same question in SQL: SELECT ... WHERE ....

fields.label: Whose badges opened the door to the service corridor between 20:30 and 21:00? Give their employee IDs (EMP-...), not their badge IDs.

hints: Import door_log.csv in Google Sheets and filter first, then read. The columns zone, direction and result each make the list shorter. Does every swipe open the door?

Filter zone = SC, direction = in, result = granted. The rows are already in order of time: read the ones between 20:30:00 and 21:00:00. You find two badge IDs. Look each one up in the badge_id column of staff.csv.
